title: Review annotations to GO:0008946 oligonucleotidase activity & children

author: pgaudet
body:
There are 3 manual annotations, 1 by EcoCyc, 2 by Reactome, see
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11guPyj8KYHC8jGZQoMLoOIvDEsLsapoIH7SVPirIsXc/edit?gid=0#gid=0

- Ecoli orn is already annotated to [3'-5'-RNA exonuclease activity](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0000175)Source:EcoCyc1 publication and to [single-stranded DNA 3'-5' DNA exonuclease activity](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0008310)Source:EcoCyc1 publication
- B1NKT1 is annotated by UniProt to EC:2.7.7.50 and EC:2.1.1.56, which seem more precise
- PDE12 UniProt summary: "Also cleaves 3',5'-phosphodiester bond of oligoadenylates (PubMed:[21666256](https://www.uniprot.org/citations/21666256), PubMed:[26055709](https://www.uniprot.org/citations/26055709), PubMed:[30389976](https://www.uniprot.org/citations/30389976)).", which corresponds to [poly(A)-specific ribonuclease activity](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0004535). 

@deustp01 
@amandamackie 

Do you think we can obsolete GO:0034611 oligoribonucleotidase activity? 

Thanks, Pascale

author: pgaudet
source_title: Obsoletion notice: GO:0008946 oligonucleotidase activity & children

author: amandamackie
body:
The E. coli enzyme is thought to be specific for 'short' oligos (RNA and DNA) and it's this activity that differentiates it from the other exonucleases. I'm not sure if this specificity needs to be captured in a molecular function term? if not then the 3' to 5' exonuclease terms for RNA and DNA will cover our needs and GO:0034611 can be deleted. Hope that makes sense...

Amanda

author: pgaudet
body:
Thanks @amandamackie 
We can keep the term if it is needed. The conflicting UniProt description made me wonder if the small oligo was physiologically relevant: 
> 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease specific for small oligoribonucleotides 2 to 5 nucleotides in length, as well as small (2 to 5 nucleotides) ssDNA oligomers. Probably responsible for the final step in mRNA degradation.

author: pgaudet
body: See also PMID:36026528 The authors seem to indicate that orn is a dinuclease https://enzyme.expasy.org/EC/3.1.3.7 ? EC:3.1.3.7 seems more correct than https://enzyme.expasy.org/EC/3.1.13.3?
